title: Build a generic Set in Go backed by a map with Union and Intersection
description: Greenfield Go task: implement Set[T comparable] backed by map[T]struct{} with Add, Remove, Contains, Len, Union, and Intersection methods.

injections.content:
package set

// TODO: implement Set[T comparable]

task_spec.prompt:
Implement Set[T comparable] in set.go.

type Set[T comparable] struct { m map[T]struct{} }

func New[T comparable]() *Set[T]
func (s *Set[T]) Add(item T)
func (s *Set[T]) Remove(item T)           // no-op if not present
func (s *Set[T]) Contains(item T) bool
func (s *Set[T]) Len() int
func (s *Set[T]) Union(other *Set[T]) *Set[T]        // new set with all items from both
func (s *Set[T]) Intersection(other *Set[T]) *Set[T] // new set with items in both

All 5 tests in set_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: Add ignores duplicates; Remove is a no-op for absent items
Union returns new set containing all items from either set
Intersection returns new set containing only items in both sets
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
